item.title: Boundary Projection Acceleration for 2D One-cell Inversions in the Scattering Limit
item.description: arXiv:2611.06951v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Efficient radiation transport on modern high-performance computers requires algorithms that expose spatial parallelism while maintaining robust convergence. One-cell inversion (OCI) replaces the spatially sequential transport sweep of source iteration with a cell-local solve, making discrete ordinates transport space-parallel, but its spectral radius approaches unity in diffusive problems, and existing accelerators such as transport synthetic acceleration reintroduce sweeps. Here we show that projecting the OCI residual onto a low-order angular space on cell boundaries accelerates convergence in scattering-dominated problems without a transport sweep. We implement the projection in a two-dimensional simple-corner-balance discretization with two angular bases: a linear ($P_1$) basis and one augmented with a quadrant moment ($P_1Q$). Fourier analysis of an infinite homogeneous medium shows that both corrections reduce the spectral radius in optically thick, highly scattering regimes, with $P_{1}Q$ being most effective. Across several test problems, including a modified version of the void-duct streaming benchmark, the method accelerates diffusive and scattering cases but does not uniformly improve convergence in streaming dominated problems. We also find that $P_{1}Q$ is a more robust accelerator than $P_1$ in situations where the flux has strong angular variation. Boundary projection substantially improves OCI convergence in diffusive regimes, and these results delimit the regimes that require additional stabilization or richer projection spaces.
item.dc:creator: Joanna Piper Morgan, Todd S. Palmer, Ilham Variansyah, Kyle E. Niemeyer

item.title: A physics-based adaptive low-rank method for 6D Vlasov simulations
item.description: arXiv:2611.07107v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The numerical simulation of kinetic plasma models in six-dimensional phase space poses significant computational and memory challenges, particularly when considering modern high-performance computing architectures. In this work, we propose an adaptive dynamical low-rank approach for the efficient solution of the 6D Vlasov--Poisson system. Our strategy is an extension of the projector-splitting dynamical low-rank integrator. The algorithm changes the rank based on physical observables (e.g., the electric field and energy) as opposed to controlling the error in the distribution function. Our approach is memory efficient in the sense that only rank $r$ objects are required to implement the scheme. This makes the algorithm suitable for performing high-dimensional computations on graphic processing units. Comparisons with rank adaptive Basis-Update & Galerkin integrators exhibit both significant memory savings and reduction in run time. We show, by presenting a variety of 6D benchmark experiments implemented in the C++/CUDA low-rank framework Ensign, that our technique allows us to run simulations with a significantly smaller rank, while still preserving the physical fidelity. Thus, the approach substantially reduces memory footprint and computational cost and enables simulations that are prohibitively expensive for full-rank or less memory-efficient low-rank schemes.
item.dc:creator: Fabio Cassini, Lukas Einkemmer

item.title: Energy-conserving scheme for a shallow-water model with capillary effects
item.description: arXiv:2611.07360v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider numerical approximations of shallow-water and thin-film flow models with capillary effects. These models lead to third-order differential equations, and we work with an augmented model with second-order derivatives. For a wide class of such models, which includes the classical shallow-water model and thin-film flow models, we develop a fully discrete energy-conserving scheme for both the quadratic and fully nonlinear capillary models. Numerical results show that the proposed scheme is stable and conserves total energy in the absence of dissipative effects.
item.dc:creator: Sudarshan Kumar K, Boniface Nkonga, Praveen Chandrashekar

item.title: Asymptotic-Preserving Tensor Neural Networks for 3D High-Field Kinetic Equations with Applications to Uncertainty Quantification
item.description: arXiv:2611.07364v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Kinetic equations in the high-field regime describe particle transport dominated by electric-field acceleration and collisional relaxation. These equations are widely used in simulations of plasmas and semiconductor devices. Typical models include the Vlasov--Poisson--Fokker--Planck (VPFP) and Boltzmann--Poisson systems. Their high dimensionality and multiscale nature pose two of the major challenges to accurate and efficient numerical solution. To address these challenges, we propose an asymptotic-preserving tensor neural network (APTNN) method. Specifically, to reduce high-dimensional computational costs and memory requirements, we adopt the canonical polyadic (CP) decomposition structure of TNNs to approximate their solutions. We show that the equation residuals retain this decomposition form, allowing high-dimensional loss integrals to be evaluated through combinations of one-dimensional integrals. The resulting computational and storage costs are reduced from exponential to polynomial growth with dimension. To improve the prediction accuracy in the high-field limit, we enhance the baseline AP loss by incorporating the first moment equation. The added loss term directly constrains the limiting flux closure to reduce its approximation error in the high-field regime. The enhanced AP loss can still be evaluated dimension-wise. Numerical results show that APTNN improves prediction accuracy in the high-field regime with significantly reduced computational costs and memory usage. For a 3D3V VPFP problem with multiple random inputs, training takes less than 30 minutes on a single GPU.
item.dc:creator: Shi Jin, Tian-ai Zhang

item.title: Randomly shifted lattice rules for SDEs with constant diffusion: error bounds uniform in time discretization and dimension
item.description: arXiv:2611.07424v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study randomly shifted rank-1 lattice rules for computing $\mathbb{E}[g(\mathbf{X}_T)]$, where $\mathbf{X}_T$ is the terminal state of a stochastic differential equation (SDE) with constant diffusion matrix. Discretizing the SDE by the Euler--Maruyama scheme with $m$ uniform time steps turns the expectation into an integral whose dimension grows with $m$ and whose integrand has a nested composition structure; both complicate the lattice rule error analysis. We generate the Brownian path by the Brownian bridge construction and handle the nested structure using the multivariate Fa\`a di Bruno formula and a rooted-tree expansion. Under suitable regularity and growth conditions, we prove that an $N$-point randomly shifted lattice rule with a uniformly random generating vector achieves a mean absolute sampling error of $O(N^{-1+\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1/2)$ and every prime $N$, with the implied constant independent of $m$. To improve stability and control higher error moments, the median lattice estimator is used. The estimator takes the median of $R=2k-1$ independent lattice estimates and achieves an $L^q$ error of $O(N^{-1+\varepsilon})$ for every $1\le q<k/(1-\varepsilon)$. We further establish error bounds independent of both the state dimension and the Brownian path dimension under an additional summability condition on the columns of the diffusion matrix. Numerical experiments show that median lattice estimators converge faster than Monte Carlo estimators and remain stable as the number of time steps $m$ grows. For models satisfying the additional summability condition, stability is also observed as the state and Brownian path dimensions increase.
item.dc:creator: Du Ouyang, Josef Dick, Ziyang Ye

item.title: Hybrid Newton-BFGS high-index saddle dynamics for accelerating saddle-point searches
item.description: arXiv:2611.07692v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a hybrid Newton-BFGS high-index saddle dynamics (HiSD) method for accelerating saddle-point searches. The method constructs a Newton correction on the unstable subspace from the available negative eigenpairs, while BFGS updates based on projected secant information approximate the inverse Hessian on the stable subspace. By combining Newton and quasi-Newton corrections, the method incorporates curvature information in both subspaces while preserving the ascent-descent structure of HiSD. Accounting for the evolving stable subspaces, we establish local $Q$-superlinear convergence of the full-memory version near nondegenerate saddle points under suitable assumptions. We further develop a limited-memory version for large-scale problems and provide fixed-step and line search strategies. Numerical experiments show local convergence behavior consistent with the theory and demonstrate acceleration on ill-conditioned problems and degenerate saddle manifolds in neural-network loss landscapes. The method also supports efficient upward and downward saddle searches for a liquid crystal model, further illustrating its broad applicability to saddle-point computation.
item.dc:creator: Jianyuan Yin, Lei Zhang, Shixue Zhang

item.title: A stability order barrier and SSP bound for Runge--Kutta methods with non-negative coefficients: AI-assisted proofs
item.description: arXiv:2611.07981v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove three results about Runge--Kutta methods with non-negative coefficients. First, every $s$-stage implicit Runge--Kutta method of order at least two has SSP coefficient at most $2s$; the bound is sharp and is attained by a known diagonally implicit method, so full implicitness gives no advantage over DIRK at second order. This extends the second-order DIRK result of Kocsis \& N\'emeth to full coefficient matrices and settles a conjecture of Ketcheson, Macdonald & Gottlieb. These proofs were found with the assistance of AI tools, which uncovered an interesting relationship between the Butcher matrices for SSP methods and phase-type distributions, and led to the proof of the second result: a bound on the SSP coefficient of $s$-stage implicit Runge--Kutta method of order at least three. The third result in this work is a proof that a third-order Runge--Kutta method with entrywise non-negative $A$ and $b$ cannot be algebraically stable. This algebraically intensive proof was also AI-assisted. This paper describes the iterative process of AI-assisted results, and presents an approach that centers human understanding and creativity in the AI-assisted mathematical endeavor.
item.dc:creator: Sigal Gottlieb, Zachary Grant, Lior Horesh, Lajos L\'oczi, Avraham Shinnar, Barry Trager

item.title: Boundary-preserving randomized neural network methods for Poisson equations on general two- and three-dimensional domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.07985v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we propose a boundary-preserving randomized neural network method for Poisson equations with Dirichlet boundary conditions in two and three dimensions. A linear lifting imposes the boundary conditions exactly, without balancing penalty weights between interior and boundary residuals. We construct the liftings by generalized barycentric coordinates and transfinite interpolation on convex and nonconvex polygons and polyhedra, and by radial parameterization on star-shaped curved domains. Numerical experiments on different domains show that the proposed method substantially reduces errors compared with the standard randomized neural network method.
item.dc:creator: Huifang Zhou

item.title: LithoSAGE: Spatially Adaptive and Geometrically Equivariant Neural Operators for Computational Lithography
item.description: arXiv:2611.08001v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Operator learning offers an efficient surrogate for lithography simulation, replacing costly numerical solutions with direct model inference. However, existing learning architectures are not designed to simultaneously provide geometric equivariance and adaptability to layout windows with different physical extents, and thus their generalization capability is limited. To address this problem, we propose LithoSAGE, a spatially adaptive and geometrically equivariant neural operator method trained on lithography data. Within its basic Fourier neural operator architecture, spectral weights are expressed as continuous functions of normalized radial frequency through a learnable sum of Gaussians. This representation preserves the geometric properties of the lithography system and incorporates rotation and translation equivariance, spatial interaction decay, and direct evaluation on different layout windows. Experiments predict aerial images from mask layouts and resist images from aerial images, demonstrating the geometric equivariance and spatial adaptivity of LithoSAGE. Comparisons with other architectures also assess prediction errors and parameter efficiency.
item.dc:creator: Ke Jin, Zhenli Xu, Zilin You

item.title: Sigmoid Tensor Decomposition for Compact Representations of Binary Data
item.description: arXiv:2611.08020v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nonlinear low-rank decompositions are receiving growing attention as a way to represent structured data with fewer parameters than conventional linear methods. Existing nonlinear approaches have focused mainly on matrices, which limits their ability to capture multidimensional structure. We propose a nonlinear tensor decomposition based on sigmoid nonlinearization in the Tucker and tensor-train formats. A binary tensor is represented by a low-rank real-valued score tensor, whose parameters are estimated by minimizing the binary cross-entropy loss. The resulting optimization problem is jointly nonconvex, but becomes convex with respect to one factor or score block when the remaining factors are fixed, as in the corresponding matrix case. We evaluate the method on several structured binary tensors and compare it with conventional Tucker and tensor-train decompositions across a range of common ranks. These results indicate that sigmoid nonlinearization is particularly effective in the low-rank regime, where it can provide more accurate binary reconstructions than conventional linear tensor decompositions at comparable model sizes.
item.dc:creator: Irina Kopnina, Sergey Matveev, Ivan Oseledets

item.title: A Second-Order Semi-Implicit Projection Time-Stepping Scheme for the Shallow-Water Equations on the Sphere Using Compatible Finite Elements
item.description: arXiv:2611.08169v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a second-order, semi-implicit time-stepping scheme for the shallow-water equations on the sphere discretised with compatible finite elements. The scheme splits the advection operator from the wave operator, applying a DG-upwind SSPRK3 method to the advection part and an $H(\text{div})$-conforming implicit discretisation to the wave part, solved efficiently via hybridisation. The scheme follows a three-step symmetric splitting: an explicit half-step, a full advection step, and an implicit half-step that simultaneously projects the velocity back into the $H(\text{div})$ space. This symmetry guarantees global second-order accuracy and confines the stability restriction to the CFL condition of the advection step alone. The time-step can therefore be extended beyond this limit by subcycling the advection step without additional implicit solves. The method is implemented in Firedrake and validated against a standard suite of spherical shallow-water benchmarks, demonstrating stable results for Courant numbers up to 1 (with two advection subcycles) with second-order finite elements, second-order convergence, and good parallel scaling.
item.dc:creator: Karina Kowalczyk, Colin Cotter

item.title: Universal Dimension Formula for Planar $C^r$ Splines at Degree $3r+1$
item.description: arXiv:2611.08178v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that Schumaker's lower bound gives the dimension of $S_{3r+1}^r(\Delta)$ for every nondegenerate triangulation $\Delta$ of a polygonal disk in $\mathbb{R}^2$ and every integer $r\ge3$. After accounting for the local vertex contributions, we reduce the remaining dimension defect to compatible vertex functionals. Apolarity associates a unique polynomial with each face, and compatibility forces differences of adjacent face polynomials to contain powers of both endpoint forms. We eliminate the leading residual coefficient using Hermite relations when $r$ is odd and an additional coefficient comparison when $r$ is even. A uniform induction then raises the endpoint powers until all face differences vanish; the zero boundary face potentials imply that every vertex functional vanishes and the global defect is zero. Together with the known cases $r=1,2$ and Hong's higher-degree theorem, this yields the dimension formula for all $r\ge1$ and $d\ge3r+1$.
item.dc:creator: Xinyu Wu, Jiansong Deng

item.title: A characteristic mapping method for dissipative evolution equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.08261v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Characteristic Mapping (CM) method is a transport scheme which discretizes the Lagrangian flow map as a composition of spatial interpolants. This adaptive approximation technique has demonstrated novel resolution properties and the ability to efficiently simulate the fine scales of inviscid turbulent flows. In this work, we construct an extension of this approach to the solution of dissipative problems, including the Navier-Stokes equations. The extension lifts a general scalar evolution equation to a path in a group of diffeomorphisms, where the semigroup approach of the CM method can be exploited. We give an interpretation of this lift through the geometric framework of optimal transport. We then introduce a semidirect product evolution technique to perform the time stepping of the map components. The map is evolved based on the semi-Lagrangian CM approach, and its log-Jacobian is evolved explicitly by an exponential integrator. The numerical scheme is demonstrated to be high-order accurate and is tested on a range of canonical nonlinear dissipative equations. By retaining the resolution properties of the CM method, the approach shows a promising ability to simulate turbulent fluid flows across all Reynolds numbers.
item.dc:creator: William Holman-Bissegger, Seth Taylor, Jean-Christophe Nave

item.title: Variably saturated flow on polygonal and cut meshes using a mass-conservative hybrid virtual element
item.description: arXiv:2611.08276v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A hybrid virtual element formulation (HVEM) is presented for transient flow in variably saturated soils governed by Richards' equation. The nodal heads are the only global degrees of freedom, and a Darcy flux is assumed in each polygonal element and condensed. The flux combines a divergence-free part with a particular field of linear divergence that absorbs storage and sources, so that the water balance of every element holds identically, at every iterate and for any time step, and that of the whole domain at convergence. To guarantee rank-sufficiency with no stabilisation parameter, the divergence-free fields are harmonic polynomials ordered by their behaviour under rotation, giving a closed-form rule for the number of flux parameters, derived on regular polygons and verified numerically on distorted ones and on elements with hanging nodes. Darcy's law is written in each element for the Kirchhoff potential, which removes the conductivity from the diffusion while the head stays continuous across material interfaces. A Kirchhoff mean of the conductivity makes hydrostatic equilibrium and gravity drainage exact on any mesh. The storage is lumped on the nodes with weights supplied by the assumed flux. All the element operators reduce to boundary integrals, so that the nonlinear iterations need only nodal values. The formulation is assessed on solutions in closed form, on published benchmarks and on rainfall over homogeneous and layered slopes, where independent solutions provide a further check. It converges at second order in the head on polygonal and locally refined meshes, also where gravity dominates, and closes the water budget in every test. On a layered slope, cut grids refined in a band along the surface reach the accuracy of a uniform grid twice as fine with about 40% of the nodes. Its structure, shared with the HVEM for elastoplasticity, suits coupled analyses of slopes.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Salvatore Liguori

item.title: Preconditioning for the time-dependent Stokes equations: stage-weighted Radau IIA and weighted discontinuous Galerkin time-stepping
item.description: arXiv:2611.08429v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine field-of-values equivalent preconditioners for the time-dependent Stokes equations discretized in time by stage-weighted Radau IIA Runge--Kutta time-stepping and discontinuous Galerkin time-stepping methods. By weighing each stage of the Radau IIA Runge--Kutta method differently we obtain preconditioners that are field-of-values equivalent, with constants independent of viscosity, timestep, and mesh size, to the system matrix. Similarly, by using weighted inner products in time to define the discontinuous Galerkin time-stepping method, we again obtain field-of-values equivalent preconditioners for the resulting system matrix. Numerical experiments are performed in two and three-dimensions which demonstrate robustness of the proposed preconditioners.
item.dc:creator: Esteban Henr\'iquez, Jeonghun J. Lee, Sander Rhebergen

item.title: Support in the domain of numerical algorithms in the education of future secondary school mathematics teachers
item.description: arXiv:2611.06938v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This article presents web-based applets designed primarily to educate future mathematics teachers in the field of numerical algorithms and, secondarily, to serve high school students themselves. The applets allow users to explore the behaviour of basic numerical algorithms as applied to fundamental mathematical topics taught at high schools. The advantage is that no software is required, and students can intuitively test how a given method works by adjusting specific problem parameters, not only by viewing a list of approximate solutions, but especially through graphical output. Furthermore, they have access to multiple different methods for comparison.
item.dc:creator: Josef Dan\v{e}k

item.title: Eddies that ride the flow: a model of turbulence with Richardson dispersion and anomalous dissipation
item.description: arXiv:2611.07121v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a divergence-free velocity field $\mathbf{u}(\mathbf{x},t)$ on $\mathbb{T}^{n}$ that is a genuine function of position and carries both defining properties of turbulent transport: Richardson pair dispersion and a dissipative anomaly. No synthetic field has carried both, because the frame that gives the first destroys the field the second requires. The key is a dichotomy: deforming a spectrally localised pattern smears it across scales, whereas pushing its generating centres forward and re-convolving leaves the spectral envelope exactly invariant --- so transporting the eddy centres preserves both cascade and frame. In the field the finite-size Lyapunov exponent obeys $\zeta(R)=h(R)-1$ threshold by threshold within the scaling range, with a sweeping deficit $\Delta_{\rm sw}=+0.038\pm0.019$, consistent with zero, against $+0.091\pm0.019$ for the frozen field on the same data, a gap that doubles at Navier--Stokes intermittency. Companion papers prove that this family shows Richardson dispersion and a dissipative anomaly (Fefferman and Mayboroda 2026), and that a scalar advected by this flow obeys Yaglom's relation (De Lellis 2026), at small Kubo number. Trajectories forget their starting point as the smallest eddy is removed: the median separation of pairs released from one point with independent Brownian kicks varies as $\kappa_{p}^{0.0333\pm0.0038}$ over 22 decades of particle diffusivity, against $\kappa_{p}^{1/2}$ for a smooth control. A scalar in the same field closes the exact scale-by-scale variance budget, four independently measured terms balancing the dissipation to 15\% over 1.2 decades with no adjustable constant, and reaches its inertial--convective asymptote $S_{L}=-\chi r$ to $0.9995\pm0.0018$ once the measured diffusive transfer is restored, while under an imposed mean gradient $\chi$ changes by 14\% over a factor 5.8 in $\kappa$.
item.dc:creator: Raul Jimenez, Svitlana Mayboroda, Camillo de Lellis, David N. Spergel, Max Engelstein

item.title: Improving the accuracy of the momentum-exchange method in lattice Boltzmann methods
item.description: arXiv:2611.07137v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In the lattice Boltzmann method (LBM), the momentum-exchange method (MEM) is widely used to evaluate hydrodynamic forces at fluid-solid interfaces due to its computational efficiency and geometric flexibility. However, when mapping complex geometries onto structured Cartesian grids, the physical boundary rarely intersects the lattice links exactly at their midpoints. This discrepancy violates an implicit assumption inherent to the conventional momentum-exchange (CME) formulation. In this study, we systematically analyze this geometric deficiency and demonstrate that it induces significant force inaccuracies, even in elementary flows where the solid boundary deviates from the midway position. To resolve this, we propose a modified momentum-exchange (MME) method that explicitly accounts for the exact boundary location along the lattice links, demonstrating enhanced accuracy for both flat and curved geometries. Furthermore, we address another critical issue with the interpolation-supplemented bounce-back (ISBB) schemes, and that is their inherent violation of local mass conservation. This mass leakage induces unphysical pressure buildup in the system, which compromises the accuracy and stability of the LBM. We propose a mass-conservative remedy for ISBB schemes that eliminates this leakage. Through a series of benchmark simulations of increasing complexity, we demonstrate that combining the proposed MME with the mass-corrected ISBB scheme drastically improves the fidelity of hydrodynamic force evaluations, establishing a robust framework essential for moving boundary problems and fluid-structure interactions.
item.dc:creator: Abbas Fakhari

item.title: A Christov Integrating Factor Method for Approximating Rational PDE Solutions
item.description: arXiv:2611.07154v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Rational solutions of partial differential equations (PDEs) are notoriously difficult to approximate via spectral Fourier methods due to their algebraically slow decay rate. In this work we discuss approximating rational PDE solutions in a basis of orthogonal functions known as the Christov functions, allowing for the computation of its spectrum via the fast Fourier transform. An explicit fourth-order integrating factor method is derived. The effectiveness of the method is tested on several nonlinear PDEs. Relative to a straightforward pseudo-spectral approximation, the integrating factor method supports larger regions of stability resulting in a more efficient scheme.
item.dc:creator: Troy I. Johnson, Justin T. Cole

item.title: Continuous Space-Time Finite Element Simulations for Biomedical Flows with Large Boundary Motion and Time-Periodicity
item.description: arXiv:2611.07822v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present an axisymmetric continuous simplex space-time finite element method for incompressible fluid flow. Compared to conventional time-stepping methods, the space-time approach has several advantages. First, the motion of the domain is incorporated into the space-time geometry, allowing for large boundary motion without remeshing or projection of the solution. Second, the method allows for time-periodic solutions to be computed directly, without the need to simulate multiple cycles. Third, the space-time mesh can be partitioned in time as well as in space, which enables parallelism in time. The method is demonstrated on an intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) in a rigid tube. The balloon inflation is modelled based on measured data, and includes a travelling wave along the balloon. The method is able to resolve complex flow features such as jets and recirculation zones. A refinement study shows convergence under temporal, spatial and combined space-time refinement. In weak scaling tests up to 960 ranks, the cost per solver iteration remains approximately constant, and partitioning the mesh into time slabs improves the convergence of the linear solver compared to partitions that cut through both space and time.
item.dc:creator: Nico Dirkes, Marek Behr

item.title: Ignoring Blow-Ups for Approximations
item.description: arXiv:2611.08208v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: It is well known that for SDEs with non-Lipschitz coefficients, the Euler scheme can fail to converge in an Lp sense. It is also widely observed that convergence fails only due to rare explosive trajectories, that distort the expectation. In this work we demonstrate that almost any method of removing these rare explosive trajectories leads to convergence in a suitable strong and weak sense. We apply this framework to coefficients that grow faster than linearly at infinity and Lennard-Jones type coefficients that explode like a reciprocal power on a compact set.
item.dc:creator: Tim Johnston

item.title: Data-driven discovery of intrinsic Lie point symmetries of differential equation systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.08421v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Discovering continuous symmetries directly from differential-equation data can reveal geometric structure for model reduction and scientific machine learning without symbolic determining equations or a closed-form representation of the governing system. We formulate intrinsic Lie point-symmetry discovery as an operator-theoretic problem on sampled jet-space data. Admissible generators are identified from a sampled determining operator and separated from redundant, solution-dependent, and geometrically trivial directions. The framework combines prolongation, sequential subspace restrictions, and a fixed nonlinear dictionary linear in trainable coefficients. A rank-stabilization preflight test diagnoses systems whose represented intrinsic symmetry algebra does not stabilize under dictionary refinement. On a controlled differential-equation benchmark with an analytically known 11-dimensional represented intrinsic symmetry algebra, the method recovers the complete represented generator set, reproduces its Lie-bracket structure to numerical precision, and approximates a known generator beyond the training domain. Here we show that explicit intrinsic continuous-symmetry generators can be recovered from data obtained from exact or approximate differential systems.
item.dc:creator: Ilker Gurcan, Kadir Ustun, Ramazan Gokberk Cinbis

item.title: Entropy Stable Nodal Discontinuous Galerkin Methods via Quadratic Knapsack Limiting
item.description: arXiv:2507.14488v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Lin, Chan (High order entropy stable discontinuous Galerkin spectral element methods through subcell limiting, 2024) enforces a cell entropy inequality for nodal discontinuous Galerkin methods by combining flux corrected transport (FCT)-type limiting and a knapsack solver, which determines optimal limiting coefficients that result in a semi-discrete cell entropy inequality while preserving nodal bounds. In this work, we provide a slight modification of this approach, where we utilize a quadratic knapsack problem instead of a standard linear knapsack problem. We prove that this quadratic knapsack problem can be reduced to efficient scalar root-finding. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed quadratic knapsack limiting strategy is efficient and results in a semi-discretization with improved regularity in time compared with linear knapsack limiting, while resulting in fewer adaptive timesteps in shock-type problems.
item.dc:creator: Brian Christner, Jesse Chan

item.title: Entropy stable finite difference methods via entropy correction artificial viscosity and knapsack limiting
item.description: arXiv:2508.21226v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Entropy stable methods have become increasingly popular in the field of computational fluid dynamics. They often work by satisfying some form of a discrete entropy inequality: a discrete form of the 2nd law of thermodynamics. Schemes which satisfy a (semi-)discrete entropy inequality typically behave much more robustly, and do so in a way that is hyperparameter free. Recently, a new strategy was introduced to construct entropy stable discontinuous Galerkin methods: knapsack limiting, which blends together a low order, positivity preserving, and entropy stable scheme with a high order accurate scheme, in order to produce a high order accurate, entropy stable, and positivity preserving scheme. Another recent strategy introduces an entropy correction artificial viscosity into a high order scheme, aiming to satisfy a cell entropy inequality. In this work, we introduce the techniques of knapsack limiting and artificial viscosity for finite difference discretizations. The proposed schemes preserve high order accuracy in sufficiently smooth conditions, are entropy stable, and are hyperparameter free. Moreover, the proposed knapsack limiting scheme provably preserves positivity for the compressible Euler and Navier-Stokes equations. Both schemes achieve this goal without significant performance tradeoffs compared to state of the art stabilized schemes.
item.dc:creator: Brian Christner, Jesse Chan

item.title: Efficient and Robust Carath\'{e}odory-Steinitz Pruning of Positive Discrete Measures
item.description: arXiv:2510.14916v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In many applications, one seeks to approximate integration against a positive measure of interest by a positive discrete measure: a numerical quadrature rule with positive weights. One common desired discretization property is moment preservation over a finite dimensional function space, e.g., bounded-degree polynomials. Carath\'{e}odory's theorem asserts that if there is any finitely supported quadrature rule with more nodes than the dimension of the given function space, one can form a smaller (and hence more efficient) positive, nested, quadrature rule that preserves the moments of the original rule. We describe an efficient streaming procedure for Carath\'{e}odory-Steinitz pruning, a numerical procedure that implements Carath\'{e}odory's theorem for this measure compression. The new algorithm makes use of Givens rotations and on-demand storage of arrays to successfully prune very large rules whose storage complexity only depends on the dimension of the function space. This approach improves on a naive implementation of Carath\'{e}odory-Steinitz pruning whose runtime and storage complexity are quadratic and linear, respectively, in the size of the original measure. We additionally prove mathematical stability properties of our method with respect to a set of admissible, total-variation perturbations of the original measure. Our method is compared to two alternative approaches with larger storage requirements: non-negative least squares and linear programming, and we demonstrate comparable runtimes, with improved stability and storage robustness. Finally, we demonstrate practical usage of this algorithm to generate quadrature for discontinuous Galerkin finite element simulations on cut-cell meshes.
item.dc:creator: Filip B\v{e}l\'ik, Jesse Chan, Akil Narayan

item.title: Overcoming Spectral Bias via Cross-Attention
item.description: arXiv:2512.18586v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Neural networks often exhibit spectral bias, a phenomenon where high-frequency components may converge substantially more slowly than low-frequency ones. To address this imbalance, we propose a cross-attention-based network that combines a multiscale random Fourier feature bank with learnable amplitude weighting. The amplitude envelope modulates the Fourier features according to their frequencies, while the cross-attention residual structure provides an input-dependent mechanism to emphasize informative scales. As a result, the proposed design accelerates high-frequency convergence relative to comparison networks built on the same multiscale bank. Moreover, the feature bank can be incrementally enriched with dominant modes identified through discrete Fourier analysis of intermediate approximations, without modifying the hidden-layer architecture. We further extend the framework to PDE learning through a two-network representation in which one subnetwork approximates higher-frequency solution components and the other approximates lower-frequency components, with a learnable or analytically computed mixing coefficient balancing their contributions. Numerical experiments on function approximation, image reconstruction, and representative elliptic PDEs demonstrate the accuracy of the proposed method for problems involving high-frequency, multiscale, and discontinuous features.
item.dc:creator: Xiaodong Feng, Tao Tang, Xiaoliang Wan, Tao Zhou

item.title: Nonlinear compressive reduced basis approximation : when Taylor meets Kolmogorov
item.description: arXiv:2601.13712v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper investigates model reduction methods for efficiently approximating the solution of parameter-dependent PDEs with a multi-parameter vector $\vec{\mu} \in \mathbb{R}^p$. In cases where the Kolmogorov $N$-width decays fast enough, it is effective to approximate the solution as a sum of $N$ separable terms, each being the product of a parameter-dependent coefficient and a space-dependent function. This leads to reduced-order models with $N$ degrees of freedom and complexity of order ${\mathcal O}(N^3)$. However, when the $N$-width decays slowly, $N$ must be large to achieve acceptable accuracy, making cubic complexity prohibitive. The linear complexity measure in terms of Kolmogorov width must be replaced by the Gelfand width, with its associated sensing number. Recent nonlinear approaches based on this notion decompose the $N$ coordinates into two groups: $n$ free variables and $\overline{n}$ dependent variables, where the latter are nonlinear functions of the former ($N= n+\overline n$). Several works have focused on cases where these $\overline{n}$ functions are homogeneous quadratic forms of the $n$ variables, with optimization strategies for choosing $n$ given a target accuracy. A rigorous analysis of the local sensing number is carried out, showing that $n = p$ is optimal and appropriate, at least locally, around a reference point. In practical scenarios involving wide parameter ranges, the condition $p\le n \le p + k$ (with $k$ small) is valid and more robust from continuity arguments. Additionally, the assumption of a quadratic mapping, while justified in a local sense, becomes insufficient. More expressive nonlinear mappings-including those using machine learning-become necessary. This work contributes a theoretical foundation for such strategies and highlights the need for further investigations to push back the Kolmogorov Barrier.
item.dc:creator: Joubine Aghili, Hassan Ballout, Yvon Maday, Christophe Prud'homme

item.title: Efficient construction and explicit dimensionality of Lie group-equivariant and permutation-invariant spaces
item.description: arXiv:2604.01975v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a practical construction of functions of $N$ variables that are simultaneously equivariant under a group action and invariant under permutations, or simply group-equivariant, valid for any finite-dimensional space stable under that action. The method applies to any connected linear Lie group: it uses the Lie algebra to build a matrix $M$ whose kernel corresponds exactly to the subspace with the desired symmetry properties, removing the need for Clebsch-Gordan coefficients and explicit symmetrization over permutations. For the groups $SO(3)$ and $SU(2)$, the special structure of the matrix $M$ yields a linear scaling method which significantly outperforms the typically exponential cost of existing methods in the literature. As a byproduct, we obtain the exact dimension of group-equivariant and permutation-invariant spaces. This allows us to compare dimensionalities and show that, for large $N$, this dimension is of comparable order to that of the permutation-invariant space alone, while pre-asymptotically it is orders of magnitude lower. Enforcing group-equivariance explicitly, on top of permutation-invariance, therefore yields a substantial computational gain when approximating such functions.
item.dc:creator: Elo\"ise Barthelemy, Genevi\`eve Dusson, Camille Hernandez, Liwei Zhang

item.title: Spherical Cap $L_2$ Discrepancy -- Blessing of Dimensionality and a Distance-Kernel Variant
item.description: arXiv:2604.21340v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a dimension-explicit upper bound for the information-complexity (also called the inverse of the discrepancy) of the classical spherical cap $L_2$ discrepancy on the $d$-dimensional sphere $\mathbb{S}^d$. For every fixed $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, this bound implies that a single point suffices in all sufficiently large dimensions, which shows a ``blessing of dimensionality'' for the associated numerical integration problem. We then introduce a one-parameter family of distance reproducing kernels for the Sobolev space $H^{(d+1)/2}(\mathbb{S}^d)$. For the balanced kernel $K(\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbol{y})=1-\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\|\boldsymbol{x}-\boldsymbol{y}\|$, a lower bound together with a random-point upper bound shows that the normalized information-complexity is $\Theta_\varepsilon(d)$ for every fixed $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$. Thus its dependence on $d$ is determined up to constants depending only on $\varepsilon$. Finally, we study the one-sided spherical cap discrepancy obtained by restricting the height parameter to $[0,1]$. We derive its kernel and Stolarsky's invariance principle explicitly. A sharp mean-distance inequality, attained by regular simplices, determines its normalized information-complexity exactly in all sufficiently large dimensions and proves strong polynomial tractability with optimal $\varepsilon$-exponent two.
item.dc:creator: Johann S. Brauchart, Josef Dick, Friedrich Pillichshammer

item.title: Vector alignment in matrix Lie groups
item.description: arXiv:2606.30868v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Many measurements in physics determine a linear transformation from pairs of input and output vectors, where the transformation is known in advance to belong to a matrix Lie group, for example the Lorentz group for the four-momenta measured by two inertial observers, or the unitary group for the states produced by a quantum circuit. Among the classical groups, only the rotation and unitary groups have a well-known closed form solution, given by the Kabsch and Horn algorithms and by the polar decomposition. We extend our previously proposed Lie algebra method from the image of the matrix exponential to the entire Lie group. We derive the projection in closed form for the classical groups over the real and complex numbers, including the indefinite orthogonal and unitary, symplectic, spin, special Euclidean and similarity groups, and we give conditions under which the method is exact for noiseless data, with examples in which it fails otherwise and an extension by a data dependent involution which is exact on the whole group. For noisy data, we bound the error of the method to first order in the noise, and we show that, for the orthogonal and unitary groups, it agrees with the least squares solution over the group to first order when the input vectors are isotropic, but not otherwise. We apply the method to an eight-qubit quantum circuit and to the rigid registration of point clouds, and compare it with Gauss--Newton refinement and direct minimization. A Julia implementation is provided.
item.dc:creator: Congzhou M Sha

item.title: Symplectic Hamiltonian Direct Discontinuous Galerkin Method for Wave Propagation
item.description: arXiv:2607.10652v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper presents a symplectic Hamiltonian direct discontinuous Galerkin (DDG) method for approximating wave propagation problems, including the linear and semilinear wave equations. Within an auxiliary-variable-free DG framework, we prove that the symmetry of the numerical flux bilinear form is equivalent to the existence of a discrete Hamiltonian structure. It follows that methods such as the symmetric interior penalty, BR2, and symmetric DDG (SDDG) methods admit a discrete Hamiltonian structure, whereas the Baumann--Oden and DDG methods do not possess this property. Exploiting this structure, we construct fully discrete symplectic schemes by combining the SDDG spatial discretization with symplectic time integrators. We also develop a unified treatment of periodic, Dirichlet, Neumann, and Robin boundary conditions that preserves the discrete Hamiltonian structure of the SDDG scheme. We further derive error estimates for the SDDG method applied to semilinear wave equations under these boundary conditions, showing the optimal convergence rate for the displacement and the suboptimal convergence rate for the velocity. Numerical experiments validate the theoretical convergence rates and demonstrate that the symplectic Hamiltonian DDG method achieves superior long-time energy conservation and accuracy.
item.dc:creator: Haomiao Li, Yumiao Li, Jiaxin Wang, Tiegang Liu, Kun Wang

item.title: A fully discrete LBRFD-IPDG method for linear fourth-order parabolic equations
item.description: arXiv:2608.19250v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a fully discrete method for linear fourth-order parabolic equations with Dirichlet boundary conditions, combining an implicit LBRFD multistep scheme in time with a mixed interior penalty discontinuous Galerkin (IPDG) method in space. The temporal discretization employs equispaced linear barycentric rational interpolants and incorporates a startup procedure. To facilitate the spatial discretization, the original problem is reformulated through an auxiliary variable. For certain parameter pairs $(n,d)$, the LBRFD method is shown to be $A(\alpha)$-stable and to possess a wider stability angle than the corresponding BDF$p$ method of the same order. Stability and a priori error estimates are established via a $G$-energy technique and the discrete Gr\"onwall lemma. The theoretical analysis yields a total $L^2$ error estimate of order $h^{k-1}+\tau^p$, where $p=d$ if $n-d$ is even and $p=d+1$ if $n-d$ is odd. The reduced spatial convergence rate is attributed to boundary contributions on $\partial\Omega$. Despite this theoretical prediction, numerical experiments confirm the stability and demonstrate optimal convergence of order $h^{k+1}+\tau^p$.
item.dc:creator: Hongying Huang, Hong Zhang, Yanming Zhang

item.title: Residual-based error control for neural Galerkin reconstruction of minimum-norm wave controls
item.description: arXiv:2610.15220v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We analyse how errors in independently approximated adjoint waves propagate into the Hilbert Uniqueness Method (HUM) reconstruction of the minimum-$L^2$-norm interior control of a variable-coefficient wave equation. The central result is an identity: the error of the control assembled exactly from any approximate adjoints splits orthogonally into the distance of the minimum-norm control to their observation span and a moment-inconsistency term generated by their interior wave residuals. From it we derive a posteriori bounds for the returned control, including assembly and solve errors, and a continuous accept-or-refine test for the network directions returned by training; under continuous observability, a fully discrete estimate separates truncation, adjoint and assembly errors. The adjoints are computed here by adaptive Galerkin neural networks, but the bounds apply to any computed adjoints. In one-dimensional benchmarks with known minimum-norm controls, all inputs are enclosed by ball arithmetic. Without truncation the residual bounds exceed the true error by factors of 9 to 115; with sixteen adjoints outside the trial class, a truncated terminal space and all inputs computed from the target data, by about 1.08 to 6.50. In two and three dimensions, including a time-dependent coefficient, the neural controls closely reproduce reference controls of the same truncation, and at equal neuron counts trained hidden features reduce the error more than tenfold relative to random features. Classical solvers are much cheaper in all tested cases, and certification is confined to the one-dimensional benchmarks.
item.dc:creator: Nguyen Gia Hien

item.title: Impact of metric characteristics of the matrix graph on the convergence of the conjugate gradient method
item.description: arXiv:2610.15393v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A model of propagation and accumulation of errors caused by round-off errors during conjugate gradient (CG) iterations is proposed, based on their interpretation as iterations of traversals of the linear system matrix graph. In the matrix graph, vertices correspond to the components of the search direction, residual, and approximate solution vectors, which are computed recursively at CG iterations. It is shown that when the number of CG iterations performed is less than the distance between two vertices in the graph, the round-off errors arising in the computation of one component do not affect the errors in the computation of another and are not correlated. At early iterations, errors propagate locally between neighboring vertices and are locally correlated. As the errors become sufficiently global, loss of orthogonality of residuals and conjugacy of search directions occurs, and stagnation of the iterative process sets in. The results of computational experiments are presented for matrices corresponding to graphs with a prescribed diameter, for Laplacians of differential equations, and for random matrices. These results demonstrate that the diameter and its approximate values, in particular the pseudodiameter, due to their low computational cost for sparse graphs, can be used in mixed-precision algorithms for solving linear systems, namely, for switching precision modes as round-off errors propagate and accumulate.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Prolubnikov

item.title: Sobolev--Poincar\'e inequalities for piecewise $W^{2,p}$ functions over general polytopic meshes
item.description: arXiv:2611.06646v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish Sobolev--Poincar\'e inequalities for piecewise $W^{2,p}$ functions in two and three dimensions over families of general polytopic (including shape-regular simplicial and Cartesian) meshes, allowing for degenerate facets. The proposed inequalities feature control by either the broken Hessian or, more naturally for general fourth-order problems, the broken Laplacian. Important tools in their derivation are a Helmholtz decomposition in Banach--Sobolev spaces and Sobolev--Poincar\'e inequalities for piecewise $W^{1,p}$ functions; we avoid the use of any inverse inequality. We provide estimates with fairly general Lebesgue exponents. Applications to the stability analysis of nonconforming discretizations for second- and fourth-order, linear and nonlinear problems are exhibited.
item.dc:creator: Michele Botti, Lorenzo Mascotto

item.title: Faster Linear Algebra Algorithms with Structured Random Matrices
item.description: arXiv:2508.21189v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: To achieve the greatest possible speed, practitioners regularly implement randomized algorithms for low-rank approximation and least-squares regression with structured dimension reduction maps. Despite significant research effort, basic questions remain about the design and analysis of randomized linear algebra algorithms that employ structured random matrices. This paper develops a new perspective on structured dimension reduction, based on the oblivious subspace injection (OSI) property. The OSI property is a relatively weak assumption on a random matrix that holds when the matrix preserves the length of vectors on average and, with high probability, does not annihilate any vector in a low-dimensional subspace. With the OSI abstraction, the analysis of a randomized linear algebra algorithm factors into two parts: (i) proving that the algorithm works when implemented with an OSI; and (ii) proving that a given random matrix model has the OSI property. This paper develops both parts of the program. First, it analyzes standard randomized algorithms for low-rank approximation and least-squares regression under the OSI assumption. Second, it identifies many examples of OSIs, including random sparse matrices, randomized trigonometric transforms, and random matrices with tensor product structure. These theoretical results imply faster, near-optimal runtimes for several fundamental linear algebra tasks. The paper also provides guidance on implementation, along with empirical evidence that structured random matrices offer exemplary performance for a range of synthetic problems and contemporary scientific applications.
item.dc:creator: Chris Cama\~no, Ethan N. Epperly, Raphael A. Meyer, Joel A. Tropp

item.title: LAMP: Look-Ahead Mixed-Precision Inference of Large Language Models
item.description: arXiv:2601.21623v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Mixed-precision computations are a hallmark of the current stage of AI, driving the progress in large language models towards efficient, locally deployable solutions. This article addresses the floating-point computation of compositionally-rich functions, concentrating on transformer inference. Based on the rounding error analysis of a composition $f(g(\mathrm{x}))$, we provide an adaptive strategy that selects a small subset of components of $g(\mathrm{x})$ to be computed more accurately while all other computations can be carried out with lower accuracy. We then explain how this strategy can be applied to different compositions within a transformer and illustrate its overall effect on transformer inference. We study the effectiveness of this algorithm numerically on GPT-2 models and demonstrate that already very low recomputation rates allow for improvements of up to two orders of magnitude in accuracy.
item.dc:creator: Stanislav Budzinskiy, Marian Gloser, Tolunay Yilmaz, Ying Hong Tham, Yuanyi Lin, Wenyi Fang, Fan Wu, Philipp Petersen

item.title: Global $\mathcal{O}\left(k^{-2}\right)$ Convergence of Multilevel Gradient-Regularized Newton Methods
item.description: arXiv:2610.35195v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop and analyze multilevel gradient-regularized Newton methods for unconstrained convex optimization with Lipschitz-continuous Hessians. By computing Newton corrections in lower-dimensional subspaces, the proposed methods aim to reduce computational costs while preserving the global $\mathcal{O}\left(k^{-2}\right)$ convergence rate in function values of the full-space method. To establish this rate for multilevel methods, we introduce a class of row-nested restriction operators that ensures monotonicity of the reduced-gradient norms across levels. Numerical experiments with row-nested operators demonstrate convergence behavior comparable to full-space gradient-regularized Newton, while offering substantial computational savings on large-scale instances.
item.dc:creator: Nick Tsipinakis, Matthias Voigt

item.title: Finding solutions with the Borsuk-Ulam theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.39092v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Many problems in nonlinear analysis, game theory, economics, and geometry have existence proofs based on Brouwer's fixed point theorem or the Borsuk--Ulam theorem. We study a common numerical approach: deform a problem with one known solution into the desired problem and follow its zeros. A constructive reduction of fixed points to odd spherical zeros makes the approach available to a broad class of problems, including finite-dimensional Galerkin systems, periodic solutions, Nash and economic equilibria, and geometric mass partitions, subject to the regularity and approximation requirements of each formulation. On the sphere, a linear projection supplies an explicit starting model with one antipodal pair of zeros. We give conditions for tracking the resulting curve, allowing turns in the deformation parameter, and relate computational work to accuracy and conditioning along the path. A family of linear models parametrized by antipodal pairs reaches every regular spherical solution from an open set of starts. This simple parameter space provides a basis for exploring multiple solutions; a finite search for all solutions needs additional coverage information. For mass partitions of finite point sets, each continuation step has cost proportional to the number of points in fixed dimension.
item.dc:creator: Oleg R. Musin
